cards.title: Hey there!
cards.english: Hey, how's it going?
cards.german: Hey, wie läuft's?
cards.audio: Hey, how's it going?

cards.description: Eine lockere Art, jemanden zu begrüßen – unter Freunden sehr üblich.

cards.question: What does "How's it going?" mean?
cards.explanation: "How's it going?" fragt locker, wie es jemandem geht.

cards.text: Hey, how's it going?

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: Man antwortet oft einfach mit "Good, you?" – kurz und locker.

cards.title: Checking in
cards.english: How are you doing today?
cards.german: Wie geht es dir heute?
cards.audio: How are you doing today?

cards.description: Etwas herzlicher als "How are you?" und im Alltag sehr verbreitet.

cards.question: Which answer fits "How are you doing?"
cards.explanation: Auf "How are you doing?" antwortet man, wie es einem geht.

cards.text: I'm doing great, thanks!

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Thanks" am Ende macht die Antwort gleich freundlicher.

cards.title: Nice to meet you
cards.english: Hi, I'm Lena. Nice to meet you.
cards.german: Hi, ich bin Lena. Schön, dich kennenzulernen.
cards.audio: Hi, I'm Lena. Nice to meet you.

cards.description: Sagt man beim ersten Kennenlernen. Antwort oft: "Nice to meet you too."

cards.question: How do you reply to "Nice to meet you"?
cards.explanation: Man spiegelt die Begrüßung mit "...too" zurück.

cards.text: Hi, I'm Lena. Nice to meet you.

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: "I'm" ist die kurze Form von "I am" – klingt viel natürlicher.

cards.title: My family
cards.english: I live with my parents and my little sister.
cards.german: Ich wohne bei meinen Eltern und meiner kleinen Schwester.
cards.audio: I live with my parents and my little sister.

cards.description: "Little" heißt hier "jünger", nicht unbedingt klein von der Größe.

cards.text: I live with my parents and my little sister.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Older brother" = älterer Bruder, "younger brother" = jüngerer Bruder.

cards.title: Any siblings?
cards.english: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
cards.german: Hast du Geschwister?
cards.audio: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

cards.description: In Fragen nutzt man oft "any" statt einer Zahl: "any brothers or sisters?"

cards.question: Which is a natural answer?

answers.text: Yes, I am a brother house.

cards.explanation: Man antwortet mit "I have..." und der Anzahl.

cards.text: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Only child" heißt Einzelkind – praktisch für diese Frage.

cards.title: Let's hang out
cards.english: Do you want to hang out this weekend?
cards.german: Wollen wir am Wochenende abhängen?
cards.audio: Do you want to hang out this weekend?

cards.description: Sehr lockeres "gemeinsam etwas machen", ohne festen Plan.

cards.question: What does "hang out" mean?
cards.explanation: Unter Freunden heißt "hang out" einfach Zeit verbringen.

cards.text: Do you want to hang out this weekend?

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: "Wanna" ist die gesprochene Kurzform von "want to": "Wanna hang out?"

cards.title: Come over
cards.english: We're watching a movie tonight. Wanna join?
cards.german: Wir schauen heute Abend einen Film. Kommst du mit?
cards.audio: We're watching a movie tonight. Wanna join?

cards.description: "Wanna join?" lädt jemanden locker ein, mitzumachen.

cards.question: How can you accept the invitation?
cards.explanation: "I'd love to!" ist eine freundliche Zusage.

cards.text: Sure, I'd love to!

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: Absagen geht höflich mit "I can't tonight, maybe next time."

cards.title: How much?
cards.english: How much is this?
cards.german: Wie viel kostet das?
cards.audio: How much is this?

cards.description: Für Preise fragt man "How much is...?" – bei einem Ding "this", bei mehreren "these".

cards.question: You want the price of one item. You say:
cards.explanation: Für Preise nutzt man "how much", nicht "how many".

cards.text: How much is this?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "How much are these?" fragt nach dem Preis für mehrere Dinge.

cards.title: The right size
cards.english: Do you have this in a medium?
cards.german: Haben Sie das in Größe M?
cards.audio: Do you have this in a medium?

cards.description: Kleidergrößen: small (S), medium (M), large (L). "in a medium" = in M.

cards.question: What are you asking for?
cards.explanation: Du fragst, ob es das Teil in Größe M gibt.

cards.text: Do you have this in a medium?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Can I try it on?" heißt "Kann ich es anprobieren?"

cards.title: Card or cash?
cards.english: Can I pay by card?
cards.german: Kann ich mit Karte zahlen?
cards.audio: Can I pay by card?

cards.description: "Pay by card" = mit Karte zahlen, "pay in cash" = bar zahlen.

cards.text: Can I pay by card?

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: An der Kasse hörst du oft "Would you like a receipt?" – den Kassenbon.

cards.title: I'll have...
cards.english: I'll have the pasta, please.
cards.german: Ich nehme die Pasta, bitte.
cards.audio: I'll have the pasta, please.

cards.description: "I'll have..." ist die typische Bestellformel im Restaurant.

cards.question: Which sentence orders food politely?
cards.explanation: "I'll have..., please" ist höflich und natürlich.

cards.text: I'll have the pasta, please.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "For starters, I'll have..." leitet die Vorspeise ein.

cards.title: The bill, please
cards.english: Could we get the bill, please?
cards.german: Könnten wir die Rechnung haben, bitte?
cards.audio: Could we get the bill, please?

cards.description: In Großbritannien "bill", in den USA meist "check".

cards.question: In the USA, the bill is often called:
cards.explanation: In den USA sagt man "check" statt "bill".

cards.text: Could we get the bill, please?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Could we..." klingt höflicher als "Can we...".

cards.title: A table for two
cards.english: I'd like to book a table for two at eight.
cards.german: Ich möchte einen Tisch für zwei um acht reservieren.
cards.audio: I'd like to book a table for two at eight.

cards.description: "Book" = reservieren. "for two" = für zwei Personen.

cards.text: I'd like to book a table for two at eight.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Under the name Miller" nennt den Namen für die Reservierung.

cards.title: At the coffee shop
cards.english: Can I get a latte to go, please?
cards.german: Kann ich einen Latte zum Mitnehmen haben, bitte?
cards.audio: Can I get a latte to go, please?

cards.description: "To go" = zum Mitnehmen. Für vor Ort sagt man "for here".

cards.question: You want to drink it at home. You say:

cards.text: Can I get a latte to go, please?

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: In den USA fragt der Barista oft nach deinem Namen für den Becher.

cards.title: What's the wifi?
cards.english: What's the wifi password?
cards.german: Wie lautet das WLAN-Passwort?
cards.audio: What's the wifi password?

cards.description: "Wifi" spricht man "wai-fai". "Password" = Passwort.

cards.text: What's the wifi password?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Is the wifi free?" fragt, ob das WLAN kostenlos ist.

cards.title: Check-in
cards.english: I'd like to check in for my flight.
cards.german: Ich möchte für meinen Flug einchecken.
cards.audio: I'd like to check in for my flight.

cards.description: "Check in" am Flughafen: Ticket zeigen und Gepäck abgeben.

cards.question: Where do you "check in"?
cards.explanation: Einchecken macht man am Flughafen (und im Hotel).

cards.text: I'd like to check in for my flight.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Window or aisle?" fragt nach Fenster- oder Gangplatz.

cards.title: Boarding pass
cards.english: Please have your boarding pass ready.
cards.german: Bitte halten Sie Ihre Bordkarte bereit.
cards.audio: Please have your boarding pass ready.

cards.description: Die Bordkarte brauchst du an der Sicherheitskontrolle und am Gate.

cards.text: Please have your boarding pass ready.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Gate" ist das Flugsteig-Tor, "passport" der Reisepass.

cards.title: Bad news
cards.english: My flight has been delayed. What are my options?
cards.german: Mein Flug hat Verspätung. Welche Möglichkeiten habe ich?
cards.audio: My flight has been delayed. What are my options?

cards.description: "Delayed" = verspätet. "Cancelled" wäre komplett gestrichen.

cards.text: My flight has been delayed. What are my options?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Can you rebook me on the next flight?" bittet um Umbuchung.

cards.title: I have a reservation
cards.english: Hi, I have a reservation under Weber.
cards.german: Hallo, ich habe eine Reservierung auf Weber.
cards.audio: Hi, I have a reservation under Weber.

cards.description: "Under Weber" = auf den Namen Weber reserviert.

cards.question: "A reservation under Weber" means the booking is:
cards.explanation: "Under" nennt hier den Namen der Buchung.

cards.text: Hi, I have a reservation under Weber.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "What time is check-out?" fragt, bis wann man auschecken muss.

cards.title: Breakfast time
cards.english: What time is breakfast?
cards.german: Um wie viel Uhr gibt es Frühstück?
cards.audio: What time is breakfast?

cards.description: "What time is...?" fragt nach der Uhrzeit von etwas.

cards.question: Which answer fits?
cards.explanation: Auf "What time?" antwortet man mit einer Zeit.

cards.text: What time is breakfast?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Is breakfast included?" heißt "Ist Frühstück inklusive?"

cards.title: Something's wrong
cards.english: The air conditioning in my room isn't working.
cards.german: Die Klimaanlage in meinem Zimmer funktioniert nicht.
cards.audio: The air conditioning in my room isn't working.

cards.description: "Isn't working" für Geräte, die kaputt sind oder nicht laufen.

cards.text: The air conditioning in my room isn't working.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Could you send someone to fix it?" bittet um Reparatur.

cards.title: Need a ride
cards.english: Are you free? I need a taxi.
cards.german: Sind Sie frei? Ich brauche ein Taxi.
cards.audio: Are you free? I need a taxi.

cards.description: Fragt, ob der Fahrer verfügbar ist. "Free" heißt hier verfügbar.

cards.question: "Are you free?" to a taxi driver asks:

cards.text: Are you free? I need a taxi.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Can you take me to...?" heißt "Können Sie mich nach ... bringen?"

cards.title: Where to?
cards.english: Take me to the train station, please.
cards.german: Bringen Sie mich bitte zum Bahnhof.
cards.audio: Take me to the train station, please.

cards.description: "Take me to + Ort" nennt dem Fahrer dein Ziel.

cards.question: You want to go to the airport. You say:

answers.text: Take me to the airport, please.

cards.explanation: "Take me to the airport" nennt das Ziel.

cards.text: Take me to the train station, please.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "How long will it take?" fragt, wie lange die Fahrt dauert.

cards.title: I feel sick
cards.english: I have a headache and a sore throat.
cards.german: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen und Halsschmerzen.
cards.audio: I have a headache and a sore throat.

cards.description: "Sore" = wund/schmerzend. "Sore throat" = Halsschmerzen.

cards.text: I have a headache and a sore throat.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "I feel dizzy" heißt "Mir ist schwindelig".

cards.title: Booking a visit
cards.english: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
cards.german: Ich möchte einen Termin beim Arzt machen.
cards.audio: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

cards.description: "Make an appointment" = einen Termin ausmachen.

cards.text: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Is there anything available today?" fragt nach einem freien Termin heute.

cards.title: Something for a cold
cards.english: Do you have something for a cold?
cards.german: Haben Sie etwas gegen eine Erkältung?
cards.audio: Do you have something for a cold?

cards.description: "Something for a cold" = ein Mittel gegen Erkältung. "A cold" ist die Erkältung.

cards.text: Do you have something for a cold?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Do I need a prescription?" fragt, ob du ein Rezept brauchst.

cards.title: I have a question
cards.english: Sorry, could you repeat that?
cards.german: Entschuldigung, könnten Sie das wiederholen?
cards.audio: Sorry, could you repeat that?

cards.description: "Could you repeat that?" bittet höflich um Wiederholung.

cards.question: You didn't understand. You say:
cards.explanation: "Could you repeat that?" ist die passende Bitte.

cards.text: Sorry, could you repeat that?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "What does ... mean?" fragt nach der Bedeutung eines Wortes.

cards.title: My favourite subject
cards.english: My favourite subject is math.
cards.german: Mein Lieblingsfach ist Mathe.
cards.audio: My favourite subject is math.

cards.description: "Subject" = Schulfach. "Favourite" = Lieblings-.

cards.text: My favourite subject is math.

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: Briten schreiben "maths", Amerikaner "math" – beides ist richtig.

cards.title: Let's begin
cards.english: Thanks for joining. Let's get started.
cards.german: Danke fürs Dabeisein. Lasst uns anfangen.
cards.audio: Thanks for joining. Let's get started.

cards.description: "Let's get started" eröffnet ein Meeting oder eine Aufgabe.

cards.text: Thanks for joining. Let's get started.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Let's wrap up" heißt am Ende "Lasst uns zum Schluss kommen".

cards.title: Quick question
cards.english: Could you give me a hand with this?
cards.german: Könntest du mir hiermit helfen?
cards.audio: Could you give me a hand with this?

cards.description: "Give someone a hand" ist eine lockere Art, um Hilfe zu bitten.

cards.text: Could you give me a hand with this?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: Danach passt "Thanks, I really appreciate it."

cards.title: Following up
cards.english: Just following up on my last email.
cards.german: Ich hake nur zu meiner letzten E-Mail nach.
cards.audio: Just following up on my last email.

cards.description: "Follow up" erinnert höflich an eine offene Sache.

cards.text: Just following up on my last email.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Best regards" ist ein passender formeller Gruß am Ende.

cards.title: One ticket
cards.english: One ticket to London, please.
cards.german: Ein Ticket nach London, bitte.
cards.audio: One ticket to London, please.

cards.description: "To + Ort" nennt das Reiseziel.

cards.question: How do you ask for a return ticket?
cards.explanation: "Return ticket" ist ein Hin- und Rückfahrticket.

cards.text: One ticket to London, please.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Single" = einfach, "return" = hin und zurück.

cards.title: Which platform?
cards.english: Which platform does the train leave from?
cards.german: Von welchem Gleis fährt der Zug ab?
cards.audio: Which platform does the train leave from?

cards.description: "Platform" ist der Bahnsteig. "Leave from" = abfahren von.

cards.text: Which platform does the train leave from?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Is this the right platform for...?" prüft, ob du richtig stehst.

cards.title: Car rental
cards.english: I'd like to rent a car for three days.
cards.german: Ich möchte ein Auto für drei Tage mieten.
cards.audio: I'd like to rent a car for three days.

cards.description: "Rent a car" = ein Auto mieten. "For three days" nennt die Dauer.

cards.text: I'd like to rent a car for three days.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Is insurance included?" fragt, ob die Versicherung dabei ist.

cards.title: I'm lost
cards.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
cards.german: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?
cards.audio: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?

cards.description: Die Standardfrage nach dem Weg zu einem Ort.

cards.question: You want directions. You say:

answers.text: How do I get to the station?
How do I eat the station?

cards.explanation: "How do I get to...?" fragt nach dem Weg.

cards.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Excuse me" öffnet höflich das Gespräch mit Fremden.

cards.title: Go straight
cards.english: Go straight, then turn left at the lights.
cards.german: Geh geradeaus, dann links an der Ampel.
cards.audio: Go straight, then turn left at the lights.

cards.description: "The lights" (traffic lights) sind die Ampel. "Turn left" = links abbiegen.

cards.question: "Turn left at the lights" means turn left at:

cards.text: Go straight, then turn left at the lights.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "It's on your right" heißt "Es ist auf deiner rechten Seite".

cards.title: Nice day
cards.english: It's a beautiful day today!
cards.german: Heute ist ein schöner Tag!
cards.audio: It's a beautiful day today!

cards.description: Fürs Wetter startet man Sätze mit "It's...": "It's sunny / cold / rainy."

cards.text: It's a beautiful day today!

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: Über das Wetter zu reden ist in Großbritannien der Smalltalk Nummer eins.

cards.title: Take an umbrella
cards.english: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.
cards.german: Es könnte später regnen, nimm also einen Schirm mit.
cards.audio: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.

cards.description: "Might" drückt eine Möglichkeit aus – etwas passiert vielleicht.

cards.text: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Umbrella" wird "am-BREL-la" betont – auf der mittleren Silbe.

cards.title: My number
cards.english: My number is oh-seven-double-two.
cards.german: Meine Nummer ist null-sieben-zwei-zwei.
cards.audio: My number is oh seven double two.

cards.description: Zwei gleiche Ziffern sagt man oft mit "double": "22" = "double two". "0" = "oh".

cards.text: My number is oh seven double two.

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: Briten sagen für die Null oft "oh", nicht "zero".

cards.title: That's...
cards.english: That's twelve fifty, please.
cards.german: Das macht zwölf Euro fünfzig, bitte.
cards.audio: That's twelve fifty, please.

cards.description: Preise sagt man oft ohne Währung: "twelve fifty" = 12,50.

cards.text: That's twelve fifty, please.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Keep the change" heißt "Stimmt so" beim Trinkgeld.

cards.title: Got the time?
cards.english: Excuse me, what time is it?
cards.german: Entschuldigung, wie spät ist es?
cards.audio: Excuse me, what time is it?

cards.description: Die Standardfrage nach der Uhrzeit.

cards.question: Which answer fits "What time is it?"
cards.explanation: Auf die Frage antwortet man mit einer Uhrzeit.

cards.text: Excuse me, what time is it?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Half past three" heißt halb vier (3:30) – Achtung, anders als im Deutschen!

cards.title: See you at...
cards.english: Let's meet at quarter to eight.
cards.german: Treffen wir uns um Viertel vor acht.
cards.audio: Let's meet at quarter to eight.

cards.description: "Quarter to" = Viertel vor, "quarter past" = Viertel nach.

cards.text: Let's meet at quarter to eight.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Does that work for you?" fragt, ob die Zeit passt.

cards.title: Yum!
cards.english: I really like pizza, but I don't like olives.
cards.german: Ich mag Pizza sehr, aber Oliven mag ich nicht.
cards.audio: I really like pizza, but I don't like olives.

cards.description: "I don't like..." für etwas, das du nicht magst. "really like" verstärkt das Mögen.

cards.question: How do you say "Ich mag keinen Fisch"?

cards.text: I really like pizza, but I don't like olives.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "I love..." ist stärker als "I like...".

cards.title: Heads up
cards.english: I'm allergic to nuts. Does this contain any?
cards.german: Ich bin allergisch gegen Nüsse. Ist da welche drin?
cards.audio: I'm allergic to nuts. Does this contain any?

cards.description: "Allergic to + Sache". "Contain" = enthalten.

cards.text: I'm allergic to nuts. Does this contain any?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "I'm vegetarian" oder "I'm vegan" nennt deine Ernährung.

cards.title: At the bar
cards.english: Can I get a beer, please?
cards.german: Kann ich ein Bier haben, bitte?
cards.audio: Can I get a beer, please?

cards.description: "Can I get...?" ist eine lockere Bestellformel für Getränke.

cards.question: Which is a natural drink order?

answers.text: Can I get a water, please?
Give water to me now go.

cards.explanation: "Can I get a..., please?" klingt natürlich und höflich.

cards.text: Can I get a beer, please?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Make it two" heißt "Mach zwei draus", wenn ihr beide das Gleiche wollt.

cards.title: Thirsty?
cards.english: Would you like something to drink?
cards.german: Möchtest du etwas trinken?
cards.audio: Would you like something to drink?

cards.description: "Would you like...?" ist die höfliche Art, etwas anzubieten.

cards.question: How can you accept the offer?

answers.text: Yes, please. A water would be great.

cards.explanation: "Yes, please" plus dein Wunsch passt gut.

cards.text: Would you like something to drink?

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: Ablehnen höflich: "No, thanks. I'm fine."

cards.title: Help!
cards.english: Help! Please call an ambulance!
cards.german: Hilfe! Bitte rufen Sie einen Krankenwagen!
cards.audio: Help! Please call an ambulance!

cards.description: "Ambulance" = Krankenwagen. "Call" = (an)rufen / holen.

cards.text: Help! Please call an ambulance!

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: Der Notruf ist 112 in Europa, 911 in den USA, 999 in Großbritannien.

cards.title: Stay calm
cards.english: There's been an accident on Main Street.
cards.german: Es gab einen Unfall in der Main Street.
cards.audio: There's been an accident on Main Street.

cards.description: "There's been an accident" meldet, dass etwas passiert ist.

cards.question: "There's been an accident" means:
cards.explanation: Die Form beschreibt etwas, das gerade passiert ist.

cards.text: There's been an accident on Main Street.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: Der Disponent fragt oft "What's your location?" – wo du bist.

cards.title: Every morning
cards.english: I usually get up at seven and make coffee.
cards.german: Normalerweise stehe ich um sieben auf und mache Kaffee.
cards.audio: I usually get up at seven and make coffee.

cards.description: "Get up" = aus dem Bett aufstehen. "Usually" = normalerweise.

cards.text: I usually get up at seven and make coffee.

cards.title: Tipp
cards.text: "Wake up" = aufwachen, "get up" = tatsächlich aufstehen.

cards.title: Hi neighbour
cards.english: Morning! Busy day ahead?
cards.german: Morgen! Viel zu tun heute?
cards.audio: Morning! Busy day ahead?

cards.meaning: der Tag, der vor einem liegt
cards.description: "A busy day ahead" = ein voller Tag steht bevor. Lockerer Smalltalk.

cards.question: "Busy day ahead?" asks if:
cards.explanation: Es fragt, ob ein voller Tag bevorsteht.

cards.text: Morning! Busy day ahead?

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.text: "Morning!" ist die verkürzte, lockere Form von "Good morning!".
